391b232892625c63: PALOS DE LA FRONTERA, Spain: Matthew Brennan sprinted to victory in the 16th stage of the Vuelta a Espana on Tuesday to claim his fourth stage win of the race.

Visma Lease-a-bike's British rider Brennan, given a superb lead-out by team-mate Wout Van Aert, crossed the line ahead of Bryan Coquard and Vito Braet in Palos de la Frontera, in the south-west of Spain.
Team Movistar's Spanish rider Enric Mas maintained his 2min 6sec general classification lead on Felix Gall, with Primoz Roglic a further four seconds behind.
Brennan, 21, held up four fingers to celebrate each of his four stage wins in his maiden Grand Tour.
"It's unbelievable, four victories here and the plan was for one," said Brennan.
Tuesday's 16th stage, running 181.1km from Cortegana, was expected to be another chance for the sprinters and so it proved, on another hot late summer day.
A five-man breakaway got up the road early on but with 100km remaining the peloton started to reel them in.
The break was caught with around 23km remaining, setting up the bunch sprint finale.
Van Aert lead out for Brennan, who cruised to a comfortable victory, with nobody coming close to finding a way past him.
Belgian rider Van Aert has won two stages himself, bringing Visma's total to six in this edition of the Vuelta.
On Wednesday a flat stage 17 takes riders 185 kilometres from Dos Hermanas to Seville, offering another sprint finale.
489a0e7374c6c8c1: WASHINGTON: Stocks slipped on Tuesday and oil flirted with US$100 a barrel prices as investors fretted over potential inflation concerns and ongoing conflict in the Middle East.

All three major US indices dipped Tuesday, kicking off a holiday-shortened week on a lower note. The Dow Jones Industrial Average closed down 1.18 per cent, while the S&P 500 dropped 0.58 per cent and the Nasdaq Composite slipped 0.32 per cent.
MSCI's gauge of stocks across the globe was last down 0.55 per cent.

Meanwhile, oil prices climbed after Iran-backed Houthis in Yemen attacked Saudi energy facilities. Brent crude oil was up 2.13 per cent to US$99.07 a barrel and US crude jumped 2.82 per cent to US$94.05 a barrel.

A resurgence in inflation has knocked the equity market in the past few weeks, in large part because of the surge in bond yields to multi-year highs, which puts central banks under pressure to raise interest rates.

The European Central Bank is all but certain to raise euro zone rates by a quarter point on Thursday this week, while the chances of the Bank of Japan doing the same next week are intensifying, which has set the yen on course for its strongest rally in two years. The Federal Reserve is also set to reconsider its rates, issuing a new statement on September 16.

US inflation data on Friday could prove decisive in setting expectations for the outcome of the Fed's upcoming meeting. Right now, money markets show traders are attaching a roughly 58 per cent chance of a rate rise.

Oil remained the dominant theme on Tuesday, but the yen's surge looms large for global markets. Because of its status as a low-yielding currency, traders have borrowed yen in earnest to fund purchases of higher-yielding assets across currencies, bonds and equities, a strategy known as the carry trade.

In the last week alone, the yen has gained nearly four per cent, its largest week-on-week increase since July 2024. On Tuesday, it was trading around 153.97, leaving the dollar slightly lower on the day.
The dollar index, which measures the greenback against a basket of currencies, including the yen and the euro, rose 0.02 per cent to 98.86.
In commodities beyond oil, the price of copper hit a record high on Tuesday, as global supply tightened with the metal continuing to flow into the US ahead of possible tariffs.
Three-month copper on the London Metal Exchange was up 1.5 per cent at US$14,728 a ton.
In the bond market, benchmark US 10-year Treasury notes were yielding 4.8 per cent, not far off their highest since November 2023.

93972442f556d3f1: KUALA LUMPUR: For residents of Taman Bukit Maluri, the annual Hungry Ghost Festival is more than a religious observance.
It has become a celebration that brings the local community together while preserving traditions passed down through generations.
At the annual Hungry Ghost Festival celebration organised by Persatuan Yee Lan Guan Yin Ting Bukit Maluri Kepong at the Guan Yin Ting temple, preparations began more than two months ago.
Observed during the seventh month of the lunar calendar, the Hungry Ghost Festival, known as Phor Thor in Hokkien and Yu Lan in Mandarin, is widely celebrated across East and Southeast Asia.
According to Taoist belief, the Gates of Hell will open during this period, allowing spirits to roam freely among the living.
The association, established in 1982, has continued the annual tradition among devotees in the area, with the festival held on the 26th day of the seventh month of the lunar calendar.
The association's secretary, Cheah Hong Kee, said the festival welcomes anyone who wishes to pray with a sincere heart.
"Besides preserving our faith and culture, this annual celebration naturally brings people together.
"Our main intention is to uphold our faith — praying to the deities for peace and well-being for everyone," the 78-year-old said.
Cheah said the temple also holds a ceremonial dinner the following day, a tradition that has evolved from practices observed by previous generations.
Another annual highlight is the auction of blessed items, including Orh Kim (black charcoal), rice buckets and prosperity incense burners.
Cheah said Orh Kim and rice buckets remain among the most important traditional items auctioned, while proceeds from some auctions are channelled towards supporting schools and the needy.
He said the festival also plays an important role in keeping younger generations connected to the community's traditions.
"Recently, I have noticed more young people starting to participate, especially in temple affairs and worship. That is a good sign," he said.
Cheah said the festival was particularly meaningful for the neighbourhood, where it was once difficult to gather large numbers of residents for community activities.
"In the early days in Taman Bukit Maluri, it was hard to gather so many residents together, but this event brings everyone out every year.
"For me, it is a matter of faith and preserving our cultural foundation.
"Beyond faith, we preserve Chinese culture while remaining mindful and respectful of Malaysia's harmonious multiracial society," he said.
Low Kok, the association's treasurer, said the prayer spaces prepared for devotees had already been fully occupied ahead of Monday night's ceremony.

The 61-year-old, who has served on the association's committee for 31 years, said the festival had grown alongside the neighbourhood's population, from a modest gathering when it was first organised into a major annual event for the local community.
"It started small, but as the neighbourhood population grew, our festival activities expanded alongside it," he said.
Low said preparations for the three-day festival begin about two months in advance, with committee members meeting to coordinate logistics and work with appointed sponsors.
For him, the festival also marks a personal journey with the association.

He first came to the temple to pray in 1994 and was selected as the "Lu Zhu", or Censer Master, the following year through the selection process, which led him to remain with the association ever since.
He said the festival ultimately carries hopes for the community to enjoy good health, prosperity and smooth endeavours, while also paying respects to ancestors.
"We hope each passing year will be even better than the last," he said.
BRINGING THE COMMUNITY TOGETHER
As midnight approached, the temple courtyard grew increasingly crowded as devotees gathered for the final ritual of the Hungry Ghost Festival celebrations.

The atmosphere was filled with chants of "Heng Ong Huat" as devotees watched the Da Shi Ye (King of Hades) paper effigy, standing some six metres tall, being carried from the altar to the designated prayer site, alongside stacks of paper offerings prepared for the ceremony.
The chanting continued as the ritual reached its climax, with devotees offering prayers before the effigy and paper offerings were set ablaze amid cheers from the crowd.
For 46-year-old Taman Bukit Maluri resident Ryan Loo, celebrating the festival at the temple has given him a deeper appreciation of the community event.
Loo was selected as the festival's Censer Master in both 2025 and 2026 after receiving the highest number of successful "Sheng Bei" divination rituals during the selection process.
As Censer Master, Loo serves a ceremonial role, leading key prayers and rituals throughout the festival.
"For me, it is definitely a great experience. I feel fortunate to have been chosen for two consecutive years," he said.
Loo, who lives in the neighbourhood, said his experience has strengthened his belief in the importance of keeping the tradition alive within the community.
"I feel that this ceremony is something that we need to keep, prolong and extend for future generations," he said.
He said he looks forward to carrying out the rituals each year, with the hope that the prayers will bring smooth sailing and blessings to committee members and residents.
Meanwhile, for 20-year-old university student Chan Sue Ann, returning to her former neighbourhood to take part in the annual Hungry Ghost Festival is a way of staying connected to her cultural roots.
Chan, who grew up in Kepong, said she continues to return to the temple to participate in its activities despite no longer living in the area.
She said taking part in traditional Chinese celebrations gave her a sense of pride, particularly when she saw younger people helping to keep the customs alive.
"Participating in traditional Chinese events like this makes me feel especially proud.
"Seeing our Chinese traditions being preserved by the younger generation is deeply comforting and gratifying," she said.
Chan said parents could help by bringing their children to temples and involving them in different activities, allowing them to experience the traditions rather than simply learning about them.

129e1f1f817d1b76: NEW YORK: Two-time defending champion Aryna Sabalenka rallied from a break down in the final set to edge Elena Noskova 7-6 (7/1), 3-6, 7-6 (10/7) and reach the US Open semi-finals on Tuesday.

Sabalenka hadn't dropped set in reaching the quarter-finals, but she needed all her resolve to withstand the sixth-seeded Wimbledon winner, who fired 46 winners, including 18 aces, in a heavyweight clash on Arthur Armstrong Stadium.
"What a battle," Sabalenka told the crowd. "I was pushing myself to the limit, especially in the third set.
"I honestly thought that was it, the match was over, and that's what helped me to feel loose and go for my shots," added Sabalenka, who trailed 4-2 in the third set.
Sabalenka's precision and power were on full display, but as the resilient Noskova fought off multiple break points her frustration mounted and the Czech's confidence grew.
Noskova had all the momentum after breaking Sabalenka for a 3-2 lead in the third – aided by two double faults from Sabalenka.

But Sabalenka dug in and eventually broke back as they hurtled to the tiebreaker – where Sabalenka dropped the first two points before climbing back, finishing it out with a fearless second-serve ace.

"I just felt at some point in the third set she was definitely serving better than me and putting so much pressure on me, but I'm glad that I kind of, like, threw that thought away and I was able to focus point by point," Sabalenka said.
"I'm happy the way I broke her serve at 3-4. I think I really played great intensity level of tennis, and that really gave me so much confidence that I still can get the win in this match."
Sabalenka must retain her title to have a chance to keep the number one ranking, and could still slip from the summit if Elena Rybkina wins her quarter-final match against Zheng Qinwen.
But after coming up empty in the first three Grand Slams of the year, Sabalenka said she would be "more than happy" to leave New York with the title and without the ranking.
Sabalenka opened the match with a formidable service hold capped by an ace.

She broke a tentative Noskova in the second game on the way to a 3-0 lead, but the Czech was settling in, matching Sabalenka's power to extend the rallies and regaining the break in the ninth game with a ferocious service return.
Sabalenka reasserted herself in the tiebreaker, but she was unable to build on that momentum as she squandered three break chances in the opening game of the second set.
DIFFERENT DECISIONS
She let another chance get away in the fifth game before Noskova broke for a 4-2 lead, Sabalenka double faulting on break point.

Two games later Sabalenka was in trouble again. She fought off a set point with an ace before producing two more big serves to cut the gap to 5-3, but Noskova clinched the set in the next game with an ace on her fourth set point.
In a match where the difference was "just a matter of a couple of points," Noskova said she could have done "a lot of things differently."

"Being a break up in the third set ... also having a little break at the start of the tiebreak in the third – it's frustrating," she said. "I definitely could have done different decisions at those crucial moments."
Sabalenka will face the winner of the all-American quarter-final between third seed Jessica Pegula and Emma Navarro in the last four.

31bc43911807a71b: LONDON: Almost 1,100 flights to and from UK airports were cancelled Tuesday due to what the country's air traffic control service called a technical issue, in the latest glitch to spark travel chaos.
A total of 1,055 flights to and from British airports had been axed by 8pm, according to the aircraft tracking website FlightRadar24.
"Recovery from today's system issue has taken longer than we had hoped," Britain's air traffic control service, known as NATS, said on X early evening.

"Our system issue is now resolved, we are operating normally and working as hard as possible to clear the backlog of flights," it noted, adding "this is hugely frustrating and apologise unreservedly".
Tuesday's issues follow a technical glitch in July last year that saw scores of flights to and from the UK cancelled and which prompted anger from airline chiefs.
Britain saw its worst air systems failure in years in 2023, with more than 700,000 passengers affected after hundreds of flights were delayed or cancelled.
Heathrow Airport, Britain's largest and busiest airport, in west London, confirmed it was among those affected on Tuesday, along with Gatwick to the south of the UK capital.

"It's just an absolute nightmare down there," healthcare worker Josie Donoghue said of Gatwick after leaving the airport, having had to disembark her flight to Ireland after three hours stuck on the runway.
"Getting through that airport was like trying to get out of Alcatraz," she told Britain's domestic Press Association news agency.
Liverpool, Birmingham and Edinburgh airports were also affected, while Dublin Aiport in Ireland said it had cancelled dozens of flights.
British Airways said it was forced to cancel or divert more than 100 flights, impacting tens of thousands of its customers.
Irish no-frills carrier Ryanair said more than 65,000 of its passengers had been disrupted and it had cancelled more than 50 flights.
Arsenal, due to play Napoli in the Champions League Wednesday in the southern Italian city, were forced to cancel a press conference ahead of the match after the team's flight was delayed.
British transport secretary Heidi Alexander said on X she was "seeking assurances that lessons will be learned and systems that support aviation are up to the job".
But Ryanair COO Neal McMahon repeated his calls for NATS chief executive Martin Rolfe to be fired, accusing him of having again "failed UK travellers".
"Enough is enough, it's time for the UK government to intervene... and put somebody in charge who can do the job."
f8f6d13bdd329bc3: NEW YORK: Frances Tiafoe recovered from two sets and a break down to beat US compatriot Alex Michelsen 5-7, 3-6, 7-5, 6-3, 7-6(6) at the US Open on Tuesday, reaching the semi-finals for a third time in a thrilling fightback.

Tiafoe appeared to have lost all the magic of his early campaign before wresting the momentum in the third set and clinching it with a forehand winner. He will next play either eighth seed Ben Shelton or defending champion Carlos Alcaraz.

Tiafoe thrived in his beloved Louis Armstrong Stadium this week but struggled to hit his stride on the Arthur Ashe court, sending four winners versus his opponent's 15 in the opening set, before handing over the critical break on set point.

Michelsen did some of his best work running up on the net in the second set, where he got the decisive break with a fine backhand strike, and he sent another shot down the line to break in the opening game of the third.

But Tiafoe dug in his heels, levelling it in the 10th game as Michelsen lost his poise, and the veteran slammed his foot on the gas with another break on set point before winning the first three games of the penultimate set.

The two brought their best tennis to a nerve-searing final set, where the crowd sprang to their feet as Tiafoe sealed the win before embracing an emotional Michelsen after closing out the four-hour and 38-minute contest.
be95d8e8751ab05d: LONDON: Newcastle battled into the League Cup fourth round as Joe Willock's late goal sealed a bruising 1-0 win against Millwall on Tuesday.
Matthias Jaissle's side were inches away from falling behind in the closing stages at The Den when Millwall striker Tairyk Arconte hit the post.
But the Magpies made the most of that escape to snatch the third-round victory in the 81st minute.
Willock met Lewis Hall's low cross with a close-range shot that trickled into the far corner after taking a deflection.
Second-tier Millwall brought on 15-year-old forward Regan Anderson to become the club's second-youngest ever player in the final minutes.
But Newcastle survived to keep alive their bid to win the League Cup for a second time in three years.
The Premier League club are unbeaten in five matches in all competitions under new boss Jaissle, who was the surprise choice to replace Eddie Howe when he stepped down in August.
Marco Rose secured his first victory as Bournemouth boss as Ryan Christie's hat-trick inspired a 4-0 win against second-tier Lincoln at the Vitality Stadium.
Scotland forward Christie netted in the seventh, 69th and 88th minutes for his second career hat-trick before Rayan wrapped up the victory in stoppage-time.
Rose had overseen draws with Newcastle and Everton and a defeat at Manchester City in his first three matches in charge since replacing Andoni Iraola.
Jorgen Strand Larsen struck twice to fire Crystal Palace to a 3-0 win against Championship side Middlesbrough at Selhurst Park.
Strand Larsen nodded home in each half before substitute Daichi Kamada lobbed goalkeeper Sol Brynn for the third.
Chemsdine Talbi clinched Sunderland's 1-0 win against Hull at the Stadium of Light.
A lacklustre meeting between the two Premier League sides was settled by Talbi's chipped finish in the 71st minute.
It was Hull's first defeat this season after three unbeaten games in the Premier League and a League Cup second-round win over Stoke.
Bradford won 3-1 at fellow third-tier side Leyton Orient.
Will Swan, Stephen Humphrys and Nick Powell netted for Bradford, with Orient's reply coming through a Macaulay Gillesphey own goal.
Chelsea host Leeds in Wednesday's third-round tie, while holders Manchester City, Arsenal, Manchester United and Liverpool all play their ties next week.
3dc154460d2b73c6: KUALA LUMPUR: Genting Malaysia Bhd's planned superyacht marina can help position Langkawi as a higher-value maritime and tourism hub, while boosting its appeal to high-spending visitors.

The project, which is expected to welcome its first yachts in the second half of 2027, could also strengthen the island's case as the home of the Langkawi International Maritime and Aerospace Exhibition (Lima), industry experts said.

This comes as certain quarters have called for Lima to be moved out of Langkawi, citing constraints including accessibility, infrastructure and the island's capacity to host a larger-scale exhibition.

UniKL Business School economic analyst Associate Professor Dr Aimi Zulhazmi Abdul Rashid said the proposed marina could complement Lima's existing defence, aerospace, maritime and tourism pillars by adding luxury yachting and marine conventions.
"Adding a superyacht adds the fifth pillar which is luxury yachting or marine conventions," Aimi told Business Times.
Aimi said a superyacht marina provides Lima a permanent "show and sail" facility where naval vessels, coast guard and maritime tech exhibitors can dock all year-round.
He described Lima as the "best marketing tool" for the marina, saying the combination could help position Langkawi as a regional maritime hub.
This will transform Langkawi from a five-day event site into a 365-day maritime demo hub.
"Lima provides the global branding, the marina provides the permanent infrastructure. One without the other is weaker.
"This will strengthen the Langkawi branding as a premium tourism spot in the region. The infrastructures are already available in the well known Island," he said.
A Question Of Lima's Future
The potential synergy comes as the government weighs the longer-term future of Lima.

Defence Minister Datuk Seri Mohamed Khaled Nordin recently said the government was exploring alternative venues, including Klebang in Melaka, if Langkawi becomes unsuitable to host the exhibition in future.
Mohamed Khaled said the move was being considered amid the need for more space and better facilities as competing defence exhibitions emerge in the region.
"Looking at Klebang, it is not far from Batu Berendam, which has an airport, and ships can also berth here. So, this is actually a location that could serve as an alternative to Langkawi.
"When Lima is held in Langkawi, not many people are able to attend. But if it is held in Melaka, people from across the country could come.
"So, this is an alternative that we can explore, although as Chief Minister Datuk Seri Ab Rauf Yusoh said, it would require very substantial investment," he said.

Former prime minister Tun Dr Mahathir Mohamad, meanwhile, has argued that Lima's international brand should be preserved, saying shortcomings should be addressed rather than simply moving the exhibition.
"We have spent decades building up Lima's brand at the international level, and fundamentally, it has been accepted. The presence of international defence companies is proof of this.
"If there is a major need to have another related exhibition that Lima cannot accommodate, then organise another exhibition that is more targeted," Dr Mahathir said in a post on Threads.
Marina Investment Still Under Wraps

Genting Malaysia, through Resorts World Langkawi, is partnering with Singapore-listed SUTL Enterprise Ltd's ONE°15 Marina to develop the marina, which will have more than 90 berths and accommodate superyachts of up to 140 feet.
Its location could also create a regional cruising link between ONE°15 Marina Sentosa Cove in Singapore and ONE°15 Marina Panwa Phuket in Thailand.

While Genting Malaysia has not disclosed the investment value of the proposed ONE°15 Marina Langkawi, industry estimates suggest that developing a facility capable of handling superyachts could require significant capital.
Maritime industry and logistics expert Nazery Khalid said the cost could range from US$15 million to US$65 million for a mid-sized superyacht marina, depending on the scale and specifications.

Nazery said a larger mega-destination marina built from scratch could cost between US$65 million and US$120 million, particularly if it includes integrated retail, dining, club and other lifestyle components.

He also estimated that deep-water basin dredging and wall reinforcement needed to achieve a draft of around six metres could cost between US$1 million and US$5 million, depending on tidal conditions and seabed topography.
A Regional Maritime Ecosystem

Aimi said the key question was therefore not simply whether Lima should remain in Langkawi, but whether the exhibition and new maritime infrastructure could be developed together to create a stronger year-round economic ecosystem.
"If Lima is relocated, the marina loses its biggest annual lead generator. A marina without Lima is just another marina. Together, they could be a regional maritime brand," he said.

d8d707cd507caaa8: KUALA LUMPUR: The government is exploring interventions under the Bumiputera Economic Transformation Plan 2035 (PuTERA35) to double the contribution of Bumiputera micro, small and medium enterprises (MSMEs) to Malaysia's gross domestic product (GDP) by 2035.

The proposal was among the key areas discussed at the Bumiputera Wealth Creation and Corporate Empowerment Forum held here on Monday, which focused on strengthening business growth, asset ownership and economic participation.

Bumiputera-owned businesses currently contribute 8.1 per cent to the country's GDP, with the forum examining measures to help them scale up, enhance competitiveness and create greater value and wealth.
The forum was jointly organised by Unit Peneraju Agenda Bumiputera (Teraju), Ekuiti Nasional Bhd (Ekuinas) and UDA Holdings Bhd.

It brought together representatives from the government, government-linked investment companies, government-linked companies, financial institutions, capital market players, property developers and the private sector.

Economy Minister Datuk Seri Akmal Nasrullah Mohd Nasir, who participated in a dialogue session with forum participants, said the existing 15 per cent GDP contribution target for Bumiputera companies under PuTERA35 should not be viewed as the final goal.
"With the changing economic landscape and increasingly intense competition, we need to reassess our level of ambition and identify how Bumiputera's economic contribution can be increased.
"This requires us to build more Bumiputera companies capable of expanding at a larger scale, competing in high-value sectors and subsequently increasing Bumiputera economic participation," he said.

The forum discussed interventions to increase the scale and competitiveness of Bumiputera companies, enabling them to move beyond participation in economic value chains and become major players in high-value sectors.
Of the 11 sectors identified under PuTERA35, seven strategic sectors were identified as having significant room to increase Bumiputera participation and ownership.
These are wholesale and retail trade, halal and food, agriculture and agro-based industries, information technology, tourism, business services and logistics.
Ekuinas chief executive officer Aliff Omar Mohamad Omar said Malaysia did not lack Bumiputera entrepreneurs, but needed to help more companies grow into national and regional players.
"The bigger challenge today is how to help more Bumiputera companies grow from small and medium enterprises into national and regional-scale companies.
"Access to capital today is increasingly broad. However, sustainable company development requires more than financing alone.
"Capacity building in leadership, governance, talent and organisational management is equally important to produce more resilient Bumiputera companies capable of creating long-term value," he said.
The forum also focused on translating Bumiputera economic participation into stronger wealth ownership at the individual and household levels, as well as greater corporate ownership and control.
At the individual and household level, the focus includes increasing ownership and value of assets such as homes, property, land, equities and productive assets to build long-term wealth.
UDA chief executive officer Datuk Seri Ahmad Fuaad Kenali said Bumiputera property ownership should not be measured solely by the number of houses owned.
He said UDA would continue focusing on providing properties that meet the needs of target groups in terms of price, location, design and financing affordability
"Bumiputera assets and land need to be developed strategically so that their value continues to grow in tandem with urban development.
"We are committed to expanding ownership, increasing asset value and strengthening the Bumiputera economy, in line with the aspirations of PuTERA35," said Ahmad Fuaad.
After two years of implementation, more than 50 per cent progress has been achieved in three key drivers directly linked to the forum's agenda.
These comprise Driver 4 on wealth creation, Driver 5 on increasing equity ownership and Driver 7 on private sector, GLC and GLIC participation.
Implementation of the three drivers is targeted to reach 80 per cent by the end of 2026.
Overall, PuTERA35 is being implemented through three main pillars, 12 drivers and 132 initiatives involving ministries, agencies, GLICs and GLCs.
Its implementation is monitored by the Bumiputera Economic Council, chaired by Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim.
Progress has also been recorded in the capital market, with three Bumiputera companies listed on Bursa Malaysia since PuTERA35 was introduced, compared with one previously.
The three companies have a combined market capitalisation of RM1.065 billion, while another two companies have received approval for listing before the end of 2026.
The developments reflect the government's efforts to strengthen financing, corporate governance, corporate readiness and access to capital markets to support Bumiputera companies' expansion.

4395f97fdedaa767: PETALING JAYA: Recent indications that Petronas and Petroleum Sarawak Bhd (Petros) may be edging closer to resolving their long-running dispute should be treated with caution, says economist Harridon Suffian.
Last month, The Edge reported that the feud would likely be settled soon, citing sources familiar with the matter.

However, Harridon, of Universiti Kuala Lumpur, said the core issues, namely the extent of Sarawak’s control over its oil and gas resources and the financial returns due to the state, have yet to be resolved.
He said that over the past two years, repeated claims have surfaced suggesting the dispute was either resolved or that a resolution was imminent.

“The current issue has not moved far from the previous contention. It still revolves around the degree of control over the rights, privileges, fields and production of oil and gas offshore East Malaysia,” he told FMT.
Harridon said the dispute also involved the financial returns sought by Sarawak, with the state seeking a substantial increase based on its reserves and production.
However, he said Petronas had rejected the numerical value proposed, arguing that it would significantly affect the company’s revenue structure.

Sarawak has sought greater control over its oil and gas resources through Petros, appointing the state-owned company as the gas aggregator for its domestic market, while Petronas continues to assert its national authority and responsibilities under the Petroleum Development Act 1974 (PDA).
In November 2024, Sarawak announced that negotiations had effectively concluded, with formal confirmation from Petronas expected. Despite this, talks have continued.
In early 2025, Prime Minister Anwar Ibrahim asserted that the matter had been resolved, with Petronas retaining its national role and Petros designated as Sarawak’s gas aggregator.

That understanding ultimately paved the way for a joint declaration, signed in May 2025 between Putrajaya and Kuching, formally naming Petros as Sarawak’s gas aggregator while reaffirming Petronas’s continued role under the PDA.
It also said relevant federal and Sarawak laws on gas distribution would coexist, with both sides to work out the framework in greater detail.
“But even that did not end the dispute. It was merely a broad political framework to move both sides towards resolving the predicament,” he said.
In January, Petronas turned to the Federal Court seeking clarity over which laws govern its operations in Sarawak, saying differences remained over its regulatory obligations.

The following month, Sarawak filed its own petition to the apex court challenging the validity and continued application to the state of several federal petroleum laws, including the PDA, the Continental Shelf Act 1966 and the Petroleum Mining Act 1966.
In March, the Federal Court granted Petronas leave to proceed with its constitutional challenge.
By June, Anwar announced that several important issues had been ironed out and that a final agreement was expected soon.
Commenting on the prime minister’s statement, Harridon said any concrete agreement would likely need to specify the gas distribution volumes allocated to both Petronas and Petros.
He added that the final stage of negotiations would be expected to clearly spell out the royalty or financial value to be received by Sarawak.
According to Harridon, the fact that both sides eventually went to the Federal Court showed that political agreements had not resolved the underlying legal and commercial issues.
However, he said this did not mean previous negotiations had achieved nothing.
“There has clearly been progress, but the rate of progress was not optimum as numerous key issues were not settled amicably, as shown by the existence of the court cases,” he said.
“The political agreements are substantially directions and instructions for both parties, Petronas and Petros, to move forward towards an agreement.
“However, the detailed terms and conditions of the agreement are intricate and complex, with several numerical values still needing to be agreed upon.”
For that reason, Harridon said recent reports do not point to a more definitive settlement than those previously announced.
3f105cf95da84829: PETALING JAYA: Petunjuk baharu berkait Petronas dan Petroleum Sarawak Bhd (Petros) yang semakin hampir menyelesaikan pertikaian berpanjangan perlu dilihat dengan berhati-hati, kata ahli ekonomi Harridon Suffian.
Bulan lalu, The Edge melaporkan pertikaian itu berkemungkinan akan selesai tidak lama lagi, memetik sumber mengetahui perkara berkenaan.

Namun, Harridon dari Universiti Kuala Lumpur, berkata isu teras iaitu sejauh mana kawalan Sarawak terhadap sumber minyak dan gasnya serta pulangan kewangan kepada negeri itu, masih belum diselesaikan.
Menurutnya, sepanjang dua tahun lalu, beberapa dakwaan berulang kali timbul bahawa pertikaian berkenaan sama ada telah selesai atau penyelesaiannya hampir dimuktamadkan.

“Isu semasa masih tidak jauh berbeza daripada pertikaian sebelum ini. Ia masih berkisar mengenai sejauh mana kawalan terhadap hak, keistimewaan, medan serta pengeluaran minyak dan gas di luar pesisir Malaysia Timur,” katanya kepada FMT.
Harridon berkata, pertikaian turut membabitkan pulangan kewangan dihasratkan Sarawak, dengan negeri menuntut peningkatan besar berdasarkan rizab dan pengeluaran dimilikinya.
Bagaimanapun, katanya, Petronas menolak nilai angka dicadangkan kerana akan memberi kesan besar kepada struktur pendapatan syarikat.
Sarawak menuntut kawalan lebih besar terhadap sumber minyak dan gasnya melalui Petros, termasuk melantik syarikat milik negeri sebagai pengagregat gas bagi pasaran domestik.
Petronas pula terus menegaskan kuasa dan tanggungjawab nasionalnya di bawah Akta Kemajuan Petroleum 1974 (PDA).
Pada November 2024, Sarawak mengumumkan rundingan pada dasarnya telah selesai, dengan pengesahan rasmi daripada Petronas dijangka menyusul. Tetapi, rundingan masih diteruskan selepas itu.
Pada awal 2025, Perdana Menteri Anwar Ibrahim turut menyatakan isu itu telah selesai, apabila Petronas mengekalkan peranan nasionalnya, manakala Petros dinamakan pengagregat gas Sarawak.

Persefahaman itu akhirnya membawa kepada deklarasi bersama ditandatangani pada Mei 2025 antara Putrajaya dan Kuching, yang secara rasmi menamakan Petros sebagai pengagregat gas Sarawak, sambil mengesahkan semula peranan Petronas di bawah PDA.
Deklarasi itu juga menyatakan undang-undang persekutuan dan Sarawak berkaitan pengagihan gas akan wujud bersama, justeru kedua pihak memperincikan rangka kerja itu kemudian.
“Namun, itu pun tidak menamatkan pertikaian. Ia hanyalah kerangka politik umum untuk menggerakkan kedua pihak ke arah penyelesaian,” kata Harridon.

Pada Januari, Petronas membawa perkara terbabit ke Mahkamah Persekutuan bagi mendapatkan kejelasan mengenai undang-undang yang mengawal operasinya di Sarawak, termasuk membangkitkan perbezaan masih wujud berhubung kewajipan kawal selianya.

Pada bulan berikutnya, Sarawak memfailkan petisyennya sendiri di mahkamah atasan itu bagi mencabar kesahan dan pemakaian berterusan beberapa undang-undang petroleum persekutuan di negeri itu, termasuk PDA, Akta Pelantar Benua 1966, dan Akta Perlombongan Petroleum 1966.
Pada Mac, Mahkamah Persekutuan memberikan kebenaran kepada Petronas meneruskan cabaran perlembagaannya.
Menjelang Jun, Anwar mengumumkan beberapa isu penting telah diselesaikan dan perjanjian akhir dijangka dimuktamadkan tidak lama lagi.
Mengulas kenyataan perdana menteri itu, Harridon berkata, sebarang perjanjian konkrit berkemungkinan perlu memperincikan jumlah pengagihan gas diperuntukkan kepada Petronas dan Petros.
Beliau berkata, peringkat akhir rundingan juga dijangka memperjelaskan royalti atau nilai kewangan yang akan diterima Sarawak.
Menurutnya, hakikat kedua pihak akhirnya membawa perkara itu ke Mahkamah Persekutuan menunjukkan persefahaman politik tidak menyelesaikan isu asas undang-undang dan komersial.
Beliau menjelaskan, ini tidak bermakna rundingan sebelum ini tidak mencapai sebarang perkembangan.
“Jelas ada kemajuan, tetapi kadar kemajuan itu tidak optimum kerana banyak isu utama belum diselesaikan secara baik, seperti ditunjukkan oleh kewujudan kes mahkamah,” katanya.
“Persefahaman politik pada dasarnya menjadi hala tuju dan arahan kepada kedua-dua pihak, Petronas dan Petros, untuk bergerak ke arah satu perjanjian.
“Bagaimanapun, terma dan syarat terperinci perjanjian itu rumit dengan beberapa nilai angka masih perlu dipersetujui.”
Justeru, Harridon berkata, laporan terbaru tidak menunjukkan penyelesaian yang lebih muktamad, berbanding pengumuman sebelum ini.
f43756c48d62b0e4: JERTIH: Ten years ago, a workplace accident changed Shahrul Nizam Kamil’s life.
While repairing a lorry engine in 2016, an iron structure weighing more than 100kg fell on him, fracturing his spine and pelvis and leaving him paralysed from the waist down.
Six years later, Shahrul has found a new way to be useful to others. In 2022, he began volunteering as a hearse van driver, transporting bodies for families who need the service - free of charge.

He started after buying a multipurpose vehicle belonging to his late father-in-law and adapting it so he could drive using his hands. Metal rods connected to the accelerator and brake pedals allow him to operate the automatic vehicle manually.
“Although I’m categorised as a person with disabilities, it has not dampened my spirit to continue serving,” the 36-year-old told Bernama.

Shahrul rarely makes these trips alone. His wife, Nor Lishah Anita Abdul Hamid, accompanies him and helps with tasks that are difficult for him. “If she doesn’t help out, it’s difficult for me to move around, especially when getting in and out of the van,” he explained.
The work also requires him to manage his own physical needs carefully. As getting out of the vehicle can be difficult, he uses a catheter and urine bag while driving.

Shahrul now volunteers under the Kuala Nerus branch of Pertubuhan Amal Komuniti Besut, though his journeys have taken him well beyond Terengganu. He has driven to Melaka, Negeri Sembilan, Johor, Selangor, Kuala Lumpur and Pahang - sometimes spending long hours on the road to collect or transport a body.

Not every journey has gone smoothly. Shahrul remembers a breakdown on the East-West Highway in Perak, while he and his wife were travelling to collect a body from Gerik Hospital. The area had no phone or internet coverage, leaving them stranded.
On another occasion, their van broke down on the East Coast Expressway 2 while they were already transporting a body.
Experiences like these have not put him off. If anything, Shahrul said the years spent handling the dead - including Covid-19 victims - have made him appreciate life more deeply.

He and his wife were initially afraid when they began the work, but that feeling gradually eased as they learnt to regard every deceased person with the same care they would give a member of their own family.
“Although I can’t walk, I can still help others,” Shahrul concluded. “As long as I’m still able to drive and there are people who need this service, I will keep going.”
55a00099529f5cf3: OSLO: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky arrived in Norway on Tuesday, the eve of the funeral of King Harald V, in a visit that will also allow talks with Oslo on air-defence support.
Zelensky is due to meet Norwegian Prime Minister Jonas Gahr Store "this evening", the premier's office said in a statement.

"We will discuss continued support for Ukraine. The main issue is strengthening air defence and assistance in other areas that are important for getting through the winter," Zelensky said in a post on X.

The Ukrainian leader said he and his wife would "express our gratitude to Norway at the farewell ceremony for His Majesty King Harald V", who died last month aged 89 and will be buried in Oslo on Wednesday.
"Ukraine has a critical need for air defence systems and other forms of military support and it is preparing to face a difficult winter," Store’s office said.
"The talks will focus in particular on how Norwegian military and civilian assistance can best meet Ukraine's current needs," it added.
No press briefing is planned for security reasons.
"Our weak point is anti-ballistic capabilities. We will grow stronger. I will have meetings in both Norway and Canada," Zelensky said on Sunday.
"We must develop our own Ukrainian anti-ballistic system".
Norway is one of the main providers of military and civilian aid to Kyiv following Russia's full-scale invasion in February 2022.
f6bc8be65df8e31f: NEW YORK: Aryna Sabalenka said completing a third consecutive US Open triumph would ease any disappointment if she surrenders the world No 1 ranking, with the Belarusian's fate at the top of the ladder no longer entirely in her own hands.

Sabalenka took a big step towards joining rare company on Tuesday, beating Linda Noskova 7-6(1), 3-6, 7-6(10-7) to reach the semi-finals and stay on course for a New York "three-peat" not witnessed since Serena Williams's triumphs from 2012-14.

The prospect of a third straight title holds greater appeal for Sabalenka than keeping top spot in the rankings, with Elena Rybakina able to overtake her if she gets a quarter-final win over China's Zheng Qinwen on Wednesday.
"Yes, I'll be more than happy. A 'three-peat' sounds great," Sabalenka told reporters.
"I'm just super happy that I've put myself in the position where I have a chance to go for three-peat, even though I'm still far away from that."

Sabalenka knows the pitfalls of chasing a third straight title at the same Grand Slam, having fallen to American Madison Keys in the 2025 Australian Open final after utterly dominant triumphs in the previous two years.
"What I learned from Australia is it's really important to shut down all of the noise and having that at the back of your mind," Sabalenka added.
"Nothing wrong about that, just as long as you're focusing on yourself, as long as you're ready to fight, basically."

Should results go their way, Sabalenka and Rybakina would meet in Saturday's final, renewing a rivalry that has already produced memorable showdowns on the sport's biggest stages, including at this year's Australian Open final.
6087c0baaeb36434: MOSCOW: Donald Trump told Russian President Vladimir Putin by phone on Tuesday that he wanted a swift end to the war in Ukraine, which would allow US-Russia ties to be fully restored, the Kremlin said, adding that Putin had supported the US president's view.

The call, which the Kremlin said lasted an hour, followed a weekend visit to Moscow and Kyiv by US envoys Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner, who are trying to revive stalled talks designed to find a way to end the fighting.

Their weekend diplomacy did not appear to result in any immediate public breakthrough although they did raise the possibility that three-way talks between Russia, Ukraine and the United States could be resumed. The Kremlin, which has said it does not rule that out, made no mention of the possibility in its readout of the Putin-Trump call.

Instead, Kremlin aide Yuri Ushakov told reporters that the two leaders had rated the US envoys' weekend diplomacy "with a plus sign" and that Putin had told Trump what he believed the United States could do to help end the conflict and given him an assessment of what the situation on the battlefield was.
Trump, Ushakov said, had made it clear he wanted the war quickly finished.

"Donald Trump clearly emphasised the desirability of bringing the conflict to an end as soon as possible, which would immediately open up prospects – impressive and far-reaching ones at that – for the full restoration of relations between the US and Russia," said Ushakov.

"In his view, this would have a particular impact on trade and economic ties, promising enormous benefits for both countries. Donald Trump is keen to see a breakthrough achieved during his presidency. Vladimir Vladimirovich Putin supported this approach."

Russia and Ukraine remain far apart on how to end the war, the deadliest in Europe since World War Two, and both sides have escalated their attacks on each other in recent months. A person close to the Kremlin, speaking before the trip by Trump's envoys, said Putin remained intent on taking full control of the remainder of the Donetsk region in eastern Ukraine, something Kyiv has vowed to continue fiercely opposing with every weapon at its disposal.

Ushakov — who said Putin and Trump had also agreed on the need to continue prisoner exchanges — said he was not able to get into more detail about what had been discussed, but described the conversation as constructive and said the two leaders had agreed they would stay in touch and speak to each other by phone again if the need arose.
He said Putin had told Trump that Russia had no hostile intentions when it came to Europe despite repeated claims to the contrary by various European politicians.
"In light of speculation regarding Russia's alleged hostile intentions towards European states, it was emphasised that we have absolutely no aggressive plans whatsoever towards Europe," said Ushakov.
"The myths being spread about the Russian threat merely serve as a pretext for Europeans to ramp up their support for Ukraine and their own military spending," he added.
8f84056d2d224eb7: WASHINGTON: US forces destroyed five Iranian oil carriers on Tuesday after Tehran launched ballistic missiles at an American warship twice in recent days, the US military said.

The strikes are the second time that Washington's forces have targeted Iranian tankers in less than a week in response to attacks on US military vessels, and Tehran vowed to hit back by targeting oil carriers near US-allied Gulf states.

"American forces directed the crews to abandon ship before the vessels were struck and rendered inoperable," US Central Command (Centcom) said in a statement on the strikes, which were "in response to Iran's most recent failed attacks."
The destruction of the tankers came after "the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) targeted a US Navy warship with ballistic missiles twice over the past two days," Centcom said.
The warship "successfully evaded the attempted Iranian attacks and continued to patrol regional waters," it said.
US forces destroyed three Iranian crude carriers on Saturday after Iran tried to attack a US aircraft carrier and a guided missile destroyer, according to Centcom.
"All IRGC attempts against US Navy warships have failed," it added.
Earlier on Tuesday, the chief of staff of the Iranian Armed Forces, Ali Abdollahi, had warned that Tehran would attack US bases in the region if Iranian oil tankers were hit.
US secretary of state Marco Rubio however said Washington would continue to strike them in response to Iranian attacks.
"Iran continues to try to hit US naval ships, and for every time they do that or try to do that, they're going to lose tankers," Rubio told reporters on a visit to Colombia.
Iran later said it would target tankers off US allies Kuwait and Bahrain in response to Tuesday's US strikes.

"We warn all oil tankers in the Kuwaiti and Bahraini ports... whether they are anchored or docked -- we warn them to leave their vessels because they will be targeted," according to an IRGC statement posted early Wednesday on the IRNA state news agency.
c36f49ed27013b8b: LOS ANGELES: LIV Golf, the breakaway tour that spent billions of dollars luring top players away from the PGA and triggered bitter divisions within the sport, filed Tuesday for bankruptcy protection.
The filing at a New Jersey court indicates LIV, which abruptly lost its deep-pocketed Saudi investors earlier this year, intends to restructure and return in a new form.
But documents show LIV owes between US$500 million and US$1 billion in estimated liabilities to at least 1,000 creditors, including star players like Bryson DeChambeau and Jon Rahm.

And the future of those popular players remains deeply unclear. The likes of DeChambeau are now faced with deciding whether to remain with the tour in its new guise, or leave and attempt to pursue the millions of dollars they are owed in court.
"This process gives us the structure and time to pursue a landmark transaction and begin the next chapter of LIV Golf," said CEO Scott O'Neil, in a statement.
LIV still intends to return next year in a new form including "an innovative, player-first ownership model," he said.
"No definitive decisions regarding the 2027 schedule or individual events are being announced at this time," the LIV statement added.

The bankruptcy filing was widely expected, after LIV axed the majority of its staff earlier this month, and scrapped its season-ending team championship in August after losing the backing of Saudi Arabia's Public Investment Fund (PIF).
Since LIV's launch in 2022, the Middle Eastern fund had poured an estimated US$5 billion into the tour, before abruptly pulling the plug.
The PIF will now provide a loan worth nearly US$50 million for the bankruptcy and reorganisation process, the LIV statement showed.

LIV's star players Rahm, DeChambeau and Dustin Johnson hold the largest unsecured claims against the tour, totalling more than US$5 million each in immediate past-due payments, per the bankruptcy filing.

But even those amounts do not reflect the future remaining contract values of some golfers, that can range into tens of millions of dollars each, the Financial Times reported, citing a person familiar with the matter.
Tuesday's statement said "the Company remains in advanced discussions with" players, including on "creating an ownership structure aligning players' interests with the League's long-term success."
"Players will have the opportunity to share directly in the value they help create," said O'Neil, in an open letter to fans.
LIV did not immediately respond to AFP request for comment on the matter.
Tour officials have previously pledged that a "2.0" version of the tour will re-emerge under new investors next season, with a shorter schedule and reduced prize money.
Further details emerged for the proposals on Tuesday.
LIV intends to host tournaments across five continents, in locations including Australia, South Africa, Mexico, England, Hong Kong and the US.
"We intend to expand our fields to 75 players, introduce a cut, and create additional pathways for players to earn their way into LIV Golf, including Monday qualifiers," it said.
The emphasis would remain on courting young fans, with live music, and team competitions which will "embrace national identities, building on the passion and momentum of World Cup-style competition."
But much will depend on whether top stars including DeChambeau and Rahm remain.
Widespread reports have linked several LIV stars with potential returns to the PGA Tour and other series, though the PGA said it currently has no plans to offer LIV players a pathway back.
Five-time major winner Brooks Koepka - who did return to the PGA this year - is still listed as a creditor owed US$1.7 million on the LIV bankruptcy filing.
Tuesday's filing confirmed LIV has partnered for the restructuring effort with British investment group BC Partners - long rumored to be the tour's mystery new "lead investor."
LIV Golf is also seeking recognition of the US bankruptcy filing in England and Wales to cover its global assets, which total US$100-US$500 million.
15f4078396f03c65: NEW YORK: Eight years after US prosecutors secretly charged China's Huawei Technologies with defrauding HSBC and other banks over its business with Iran, the case is finally heading for trial.

Huawei also faces charges of conspiring to steal trade secrets from five US technology companies, and is accused of lying about its dealings in North Korea and supplying surveillance equipment to Iran to track protesters during 2009 anti-government demonstrations in Tehran. Jury selection began on Tuesday in federal court in Brooklyn, New York.

The trial will bring to a close one of the US government's earliest and most closely watched battles against a Chinese company. The case will play out as tech competition heats up between the two countries and Washington seeks to prevent American technology from aiding Beijing's military. The US-China tech war has now spread across multiple technology sectors, including artificial intelligence.
The saga began in 2018 with the arrest of Huawei chief financial officer Meng Wanzhou in Vancouver, which sparked a diplomatic crisis involving the US, China and Canada.

Convictions on the Iran-related charges would bolster Washington's case for having placed Huawei, one of China's leading technology companies, on a US trade blacklist in 2019, citing alleged criminal conduct that threatened national security.

The trial before US district judge Ann Donnelly in Brooklyn, New York, is expected to last about three months and overlap with Chinese President Xi Jinping's Sept 24 meeting with President Donald Trump in Washington. Potential jurors have filled out 27-page questionnaires, including about their views on China's and Iran's governments.
Other charges include violating US sanctions against Iran, money laundering, racketeering, wire fraud and obstruction. Huawei has pleaded not guilty to all charges and denied any wrongdoing.
The criminal case is based in part on reporting by Reuters in 2012 and 2013 about close ties between Huawei and Skycom, a firm that operated in Iran.

Reuters reported that Skycom had offered to sell at least €1.3 million worth of embargoed Hewlett-Packard computer equipment to Iran's largest mobile-phone operator in 2010. Reuters also reported that Meng had served on Skycom's board of directors between February 2008 and April 2009.
Undermining Chinese tech

Beijing has long criticised the case, saying it was part of a bigger campaign against China's technological rise. A Huawei spokesman said in a statement on Saturday, "The government's overarching narrative is demonstrably false."

Today Huawei is a centerpiece of China's AI chip ambitions, and has diversified beyond network gear and smartphones. It has described the criminal case as an effort to undermine its competitiveness and the theft accusations as a repackaging of long-resolved commercial disputes.

If Huawei is convicted, prosecutors will seek the forfeiture of property or proceeds obtained from its illegal activity. Should the company be found guilty on all counts, experts said it could face a significant financial penalty.

“The penalty is going to be determined by the benefit to the company and then multiplied by how serious the wrongdoing is -- and that could range from hundreds of millions to billions of dollars,” said Todd Haugh, a professor of business law at Indiana University Kelley School of Business.
If there's a guilty verdict, he added, “a big fight is going to be proving how much Huawei benefited from their criminal behavior.”

The case against the company was brought during the first Trump administration, which also took actions to curb the use of Huawei equipment in the U.S. and pressed other countries to drop Huawei from their telecommunications networks, saying China could use its equipment for espionage.
The indictment covers alleged wrongdoing between about 1999 and 2020.

It accuses Huawei of using Skycom to obtain embargoed US goods, technology and services for Huawei's Iran-based business, and to move money out of that country through the international banking system.

The US said one bank, which was not named in the indictment but which sources and documents reviewed by Reuters identified as HSBC, cleared more than US$100 million worth of US-dollar transactions related to Skycom.

Prosecutors accused Meng of misrepresenting Huawei's ownership and control of Skycom in a presentation to an HSBC executive. She later admitted the statements were false, as part of an agreement with prosecutors to drop the charges against her.
83bd4be158f3f5d6: MADRID: Lionel Messi is close to completing a deal to buy Spanish second-tier club CD Eldense, adding to his growing portfolio of football ownership interests, according to multiple reports in Spain.
Messi has agreed in principle to acquire all the shares held by majority owner TH Soluciones Group SAS, with an announcement expected in the coming days, the reports said.

The Colombian investment group, which took control of Eldense in October, 2025, would transfer its entire stake to Messi. The deal remains subject to the approval of Spain's High Council for Sports (CSD).
Reuters has contacted TH Soluciones and Eldense for comment.
Messi, who recently retired from international duty with Argentina, acquired fifth-tier Spanish side UE Cornella on April 16.
He is also due to receive a stake in Major League Soccer club Inter Miami, once his playing contract with the team ends.
Eldense are based in Elda, a town of about 55,000 people in the eastern Spanish province of Alicante.
The club have spent most of their history in Spain's lower divisions but, following fresh investment, have played in the second tier in three of the past four seasons.
Eldense sacked manager Claudio Barragan on Sunday after taking two points from their opening four league matches, leaving them third from bottom.
58ae2eb168843b67: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 9 — Umno’s general assembly begins today with the party facing a question that has become increasingly difficult to avoid: what does it want to be when the next general election arrives?

The four-day gathering at the World Trade Centre Kuala Lumpur comes after Umno’s electoral gains in Johor and Negeri Sembilan, a push to rebuild its ranks through the Rumah Bangsa initiative and growing questions over whether its partnership with Pakatan Harapan (PH) can hold until the next general election.
It is also the party’s second general assembly this year. The gathering held in January was the postponed 2025 assembly, making this the first regular PAU of 2026.

Umno secretary-general Datuk Asyraf Wajdi Dusuki said delegates would be free to table motions on the party’s political direction and its cooperation with the unity government, putting the grassroots debate among the key things to watch at the four-day assembly.
Asyraf has also described the annual gathering as Umno’s “Hari Raya” — a time for its grassroots to come together.
But the assembly comes at a consequential juncture for Umno.

Its recent electoral successes have given the party renewed confidence, while its position in the unity government has become increasingly complicated by competing political interests within the coalition.
Three issues that are likely to loom over PAU 2026.
1. Rumah Bangsa and Malay unity
If there was one defining political message from Umno’s last assembly, it was the call to rebuild the party’s house.

Rumah Bangsa was unveiled as an effort to bring back former members and broaden Umno’s appeal, with party president Datuk Seri Ahmad Zahid Hamidi repeatedly stressing that the party’s doors remained open.
Eight months on, the initiative has become more than a slogan.
Umno said in June that 21,858 new and returning members had joined through the initiative, including former members of other Malay-based parties.

Party leaders have framed Rumah Bangsa as an effort to bring Malays together under one political roof, with Umno supreme council member Datuk Seri Ahmad Maslan describing its approach as “forgive and forget”.
The initiative has also opened the door to former leaders and members, reinforcing the idea that Umno wants to reclaim political ground lost during years of fragmentation within the Malay electorate.
That message is likely to continue at PAU 2026.
The message of Malay-Muslim unity is also likely to feature prominently, particularly as Umno’s ties with PAS have warmed following their cooperation in Negeri Sembilan.
